newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Gazprom foreign, local shares jumping.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Gazprom foreign, local shares jumping.

text.p: Local and foreign-trading shares in Russian natural gas producer Gazprom had gained around 30 percent over the past month by Friday in a red-hot performance shaking off months of lethargy.

Local Gazprom shares, whose price teetered around the $0.60 level on the main Russian Trading System (RTS) during months of government deliberation over regulation of the company earlier this year, closed at $0.965 on the Moscow Stock Exchange on Friday, dealers said.
Only a week ago Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev said he was not satisfied with Gazprom's price and trade volumes, which are well under $1 million daily, on local stock markets.
Gazprom was delisted from the over-the-counter type RTS, where trade volumes were in the millions of dollars daily, on July 3.
The government, in an effort to tighten control over the prize company, said Gazprom shares could be sold only on "organised markets" -- including the Moscow exchange.
Non-residents are legally allowed to buy Gazprom only in the form of foreign-trading American Depositary Shares (or Receipts), each of which covers 10 underlying shares.
The ADR climbed to around $19.90 on the London Stock Exchange on Friday from $17.20 at Monday's close.

Russian media said this week a jump in Gazprom's price on the Moscow Stock Exchange, which is one of only two exchanges where Gazprom currently trades, could have been due to a Western investor using legal loopholes to buy the shares.
Most traders saw such a scenario as unlikely, although not impossible, while one trader said a Moscow brokerage had bought up most of the shares on offer at an auction on Wednesday.
One trader said Gazprom might be buying its own shares.

But they pointed to the gap between the price of Gazprom, the world's largest natural gas producer, and other "blue chips" like LUKoil, and the weak gains Gazprom stock has made in comparison to such stocks as a more likely value driver.

"Gazprom has always been a good stock, it has just had bad rules of trade," said Trinfiko brokerage's trader Ilya Galtsov. "Local shares have to catch up with ADR price sooner or later -- this is a natural process of growth."
Gazprom's ADR price has also risen strongly in recent weeks, from $15.825 on July 21. It closed its first day of trade last October 22 at $18.50.
But Creditanstalt Grant director of sales Tad Berger said they were not moving as nimbly as local shares.

"The local market is outpacing the ADRs - ADRs trade at a higher valuation than local shares so we're seeing accretion towards equivalent value, although they are not there yet obviously," Berger said, adding he did not see a special reason for Gazprom ADSs to move up.
"After the local market shares were not available to foreigners they started buying the ADRs," Berger said. "But the Russian market is up so ADRs should follow."

LUKoil LKOH.RTS traded at around $28.00 on Friday, up from around $15.00 in May, while Gazprom last traded on the RTS at $0.586 on July 2, falling from around $0.644 in May on uncertainty about the fate of trade in shares of the company.
"Gazprom is popular with Russian banks -- many of them are buying it right now," said Rossiisky Kredit Bank trader Igor Voronin.
"The attractivenes of the stock lies in the fact that it is very undervalued and its real price is much higher. A lot of banks want to see Gazprom in their long term portfolio.
--Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
